answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text: Consequential accounting is a much more precise approach to evaluating actual GES reduction of an electricity project. But it’s necessary to consider complexity and availability of the data to guarantee the feasibility of the calculation by all types of stakeholders (small companies as well as large companies).

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text: We think that summing impacts for the lifetime of the project is not accurate, since the reality might me very different, depending on how the whole power system changes year after year. Limiting the analysis to the reporting year period sticks much more to the reality.

answers.label: Secondary effects to consider, and how
Why secondary effects should be excluded
answers.text: In the majority of cases, the secondary effects will be one-time effects with low impacts on the lifetime of the project. It’s better to focus the calculation of the impacts on emissions during operation, taking into account the grid and the other production systems without adding other complexity.

answers.label: Why annual or lifetime reporting
answers.text: Reporting each years allow to take into account the actual evolution of the power system (other renewable sources, addition of grid scale storage…)

answers.label: Requiredness of the financial analysis test
Requiredness of the common practice test
Why selected tests should be included
answers.text:
Regulatory test Optionnal: There is no reason to forbid subsidies when there is an extracost due to the regulation. But is has to be limited to cases where there is an actual extracost.
Timing test Required: The subsidies is made to influence the decision process !
Financial analysis test Required: It prevents from using public money for already bankable projects.
Barrier test Required: Innovation deserves to be supported by subsidies

answers.label: Additionality tests missing from the framework
Claims possible under different test approaches
Details on operating margin methodologies
answers.text:
About SCED : precise and appropriate, but requires having all the data. The locational SCED methods seems to be more precise than fuel-on-the margin which is more global.
Scenario modelling seems to be too complicated.
Heat rate/LMP : why not when no other data is available.
Diffrence based: no opinion.

answers.label: Details on build margin methodologies
answers.text:
Recent capacity additions: not appropriate. too much focused on the past
Policy scenario : appropriate and simple
Capacity expansion modelling : best method if all the data are available
Average emission rate : not precise enough

answers.label: Assessing model applicability to project types
Other appropriate emission rates or metrics
Why that spatial granularity ceiling
answers.text: Considering Country or Grid region would be unrealistic to have a precise assessment. Balancing area seems to be the appropriate and feasible level since it is an operational level where physical actions take place.

answers.label: Why that temporal granularity ceiling
answers.text: Daily would be not precise enough for solar production

answers.label: Appropriate margin weighting approaches
selections: GHG Protocol Guidelines for Quantifying GHG Reductions from Grid-connected Electricity Projects

answers.label: Why selected weighting approaches are appropriate
answers.text:
GHG Protocol Guidelines for Quantifying GHG Reductions from Grid-connected Electricity Projects seems to be the best and most precise approach, since it considers precisely the firm power provided by the project. The UNFCCC CDM Tool is almost the same, but with default conditions simpler. Thus it's also a good approach even if it is less precise for the default approach.
The Intervention lifecycle approaches is simple and makes sense. But it assumes that the planification is really scientific and not influenced by political considerations. That's why we consider it not appropriate.
